findings.title: Denial cache blocks grants for the full TTL
findings.body: Check consults permDenialCache before both the permission cache and the new DB refresh, and on a DB deny it stores a 30s denial keyed by namespace/user/action/name/parent (lines 153-155) without ever deleting that entry when a later query would allow. Any Check that was denied for that tuple — the usual case before a share, role change, or retry after creating access — keeps returning Allowed=false until shortCacheTTL, even if the DB (and perm cache) now grant the resource. That reintroduces the staleness this PR is meant to remove, and it fails closed for up to 30 seconds after a real permission grant.

findings.title: List still serves stale permission cache
findings.body: List returns as soon as getCachedIdentityPermissions hits and never re-reads the DB when the cached scope map is missing a newly granted dashboard or folder. Only a total cache miss refreshes. Check was changed to fall through to the DB when the cached scopes do not allow the resource, but listing is the path that actually fetches dashboards and folders, so a creator (or anyone granted access) still omits the new resource for the permission-cache TTL (30s) if that action was cached before the grant. A prior Check can accidentally refresh the shared perm cache, but a list-only request will not.

findings.title: Slow permission fetch overwrites newer cache and plants a denial
findings.body: getUserPermissions no longer reads the cache and always writes permCache at the end of its singleflight callback. Check decides to refresh based on a snapshot taken before that call, then on deny writes permDenialCache. A request that started a DB read against old permissions can finish after another request has already cached the post-grant scopes, overwrite permCache with the older map, and set a denial for the new resource. Later Checks hit that denial first and stay denied for shortCacheTTL even though a fresher result was already known.

findings.title: Denial-cache test does not override an allow
findings.body: TestService_CacheCheck "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" comments that permCache allows dash1 so the denial short-circuit is proven, but it stores map["dashboards:uid:dash1"]=false. checkPermission treats a false value as no grant, so the test would still deny if the denial lookup were removed. It never shows that a real cached allow is ignored, nor that a grant after a cached deny is honored.
